title: Why Earning $300M Wasn't Enough to Save Him

beats.say: He earned $300,000,000 in the ring, yet ended up completely bankrupt.
beats.visual: Cinematic medium shot of a pair of heavy leather boxing gloves hanging from a rusty metal locker hook, dramatic low-key lighting.

beats.say: Here's the exact psychological trap that destroyed his massive fortune, and how you can avoid it.
beats.visual: A close-up shot of hands counting a massive stack of dirty hundred-dollar bills on a dark wooden table, moody lighting.

beats.say: In 2003, the world's most feared heavyweight boxer filed for bankruptcy, drowning in millions of debt.
beats.visual: A low-angle shot of a courthouse staircase, tall concrete columns, cinematic shadow casting over the steps, gloomy atmosphere.

beats.say: He didn't lose his massive fortune on complex stock market crashes or bad business deals.
beats.visual: Close-up of a high-end luxury watch on a wrist, resting against a dark leather steering wheel, blurred background.

beats.say: He simply spent it. $140,000 on white Siberian tigers. $2,000,000 on a solid gold bathtub.
beats.visual: A cinematic shot of a sleek, modern bathroom featuring a gleaming, solid gold bathtub reflecting warm, soft spotlights.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions: a high income is never the same as wealth.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a man looking out of a high-rise penthouse window at a sprawling city skyline at dusk, moody blue lighting.

beats.say: Income is just cash flowing in, but wealth is the amount of cash you actually keep.
beats.visual: A top-down shot of a clean, minimalist desk with a vintage leather wallet and a few scattered gold coins, cinematic lighting.

beats.say: Without a system to automate your savings, your lifestyle will naturally rise to match your paycheck.
beats.visual: A close-up shot of a luxury sports car's dashboard with a glowing speedometer, focus on the hand gripping the leather gear shifter.

beats.say: A heavy monthly deficit hurts just as bad when you are earning millions of dollars a year.
beats.visual: A wide shot of an empty luxury mansion hallway, marble floors, sunlight streaming through tall windows creating long shadows.

beats.say: You must learn how to play financial defense, or you'll constantly run on a treadmill.
beats.visual: A close-up of a person's hands carefully writing numbers in a sleek leather-bound ledger under a soft desk lamp.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you, so you can build true financial freedom,
beats.visual: A low-angle silhouette of a person standing on top of a rocky hill looking at the sunrise, warm cinematic orange glow.

beats.say: because if you don't build a system to keep your money, you'll never understand how
beats.visual: A close-up of a vintage key turning slowly inside a heavy brass lock, cinematic depth of field.

caption: Earning millions won't save you if you don't know how to keep it. The brutal truth about income versus wealth.
description: Mike Tyson's 2003 bankruptcy filing is a classic case study of how a massive income cannot survive without a financial defense system. Wealth isn't what you earn—it is what you keep.
first_comment: Do you think it is harder to earn a lot of money, or to actually keep it once you have it?

facts.claim: Mike Tyson filed for bankruptcy in 2003 after earning $300 million.
facts.basis: Mike Tyson filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in August 2003 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court, listing over $23 million in debt against estimated career earnings of over $300 million.

facts.claim: He spent $140,000 on white Siberian tigers and $2,000,000 on a solid gold bathtub.
facts.basis: Court records and public interviews confirmed Tyson's purchase of Siberian tigers and a 24-karat gold bathtub as part of his high-profile luxury spending habits.
